national_raw_news.title: 21 mins ago | National 20 PM Modi holds 15 bilateral meetings with world leaders, besides engagements with heads of interna...
national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi held a series of high-level bilateral engagements on the sidelines of the BRICS Summit in New Delhi. Over the past three days, Mr Modi held 15 meetings with heads of state and government, besides several pull-aside meetings with world leaders and heads of international institutions. The meetings provided an opportunity to strengthen bilateral ties, discuss issues of mutual interest and exchange views on regional and global developments. The Prime Minister today held bilateral talks with leaders of Kazakhstan, Egypt, Indonesia and Philippines, South Africa, Burundi, Nigeria and Uganda. The Prime Minister met President of Kazakhstan Kassym-Jomart Tokayev. The two leaders reviewed cooperation in a range of areas, including politics, trade, defence and security, connectivity, energy, critical minerals, emerging technologies, the creative economy and people-to-people ties. The Prime Minister also held a meeting with Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi and Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto. Mr. Modi also held talks with Philippines President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. He welcomed the Philippines’ decision to join the Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure. During his meeting with South African President Cyril Ramaphosa, Mr. Modi reviewed the full range of the India-South Africa Strategic Partnership. Mr. Modi also met Nigerian Vice President Kashim Shettima. Yesterday, Mr Modi held bilateral meetings with leaders from Ethiopia, Malaysia, UAE, Vietnam and China. On Friday, the Prime Minister met leaders from Russia and Iran and also UN Secretary General.

national_raw_news.title: Lab-Grown Diamonds Offer Monumental Opportunity for India: Amit Shah 5 hours ago 54
national_raw_news.content: Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Amit Shah today called upon the Indian gems and jewellery industry to ensure that the entire ecosystem and manufacturing chain of lab-grown diamonds remain firmly in Indian hands. Addressing the 52nd India Gems and Jewellery Awards ceremony in Mumbai, Mr. Shah said the nature of the diamond trade is changing with the emergence of lab-grown diamonds. He said the lab-grown diamond market, in terms of volume, is expected to become nearly 50 times the size of the current diamond market, describing it as a monumental opportunity for India. The Minister said India has the infrastructure, capabilities, capital and entrepreneurial talent needed to seize this opportunity. He urged the industry to build capabilities across the entire value chain, including manufacturing machinery, diamond production, jewellery making, branding and setting up showrooms of Indian companies in cities across the world. Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis, Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde and other dignitaries were present at the event. Earlier in the day, Home Minister inaugurated a specially curated exhibition of manuscripts titled “Shri Ganesh Dnyanarati” at the Asiatic Society of Mumbai. Addressing the gathering, Mr. Shah said India has a rich and vibrant knowledge tradition whose light has the potential to guide the entire world. He said this enduring legacy of knowledge has enabled the country to preserve its identity and civilisational continuity despite centuries of foreign invasions. Mr. Shah said the spirit of Bharat could never be enslaved because its memory remained alive in its history, language, culture, archives and traditions. He urged the Asiatic Society to use modern technology to take its vast repository of knowledge to people across the country. The Union Minister also visited the library and inspected the work being carried out at the Society’s manuscript conservation laboratory. Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis, Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde and other dignitaries were present at the event.

national_raw_news.title: Mizoram's Bairabi-Sairang rail line completes one year, records over 15 lakh passengers
national_raw_news.content: Mizoram’s Bairabi-Sairang rail line completes one year, records over 15 lakh passengers | MorungExpress | morungexpress.com Mizoram’s Bairabi-Sairang rail line completes one year, records over 15 lakh passengers A bridge on the Bairabi-Sairang railway line, which extends the national rail network into Mizoram’s hilly terrain. (Photo Courtesy: Ministry of Railways/PIB) North-East 13th September 2026 Aizawl, September 13 (MExN): The 51.38-km Bairabi-Sairang railway line in Mizoram has completed one year of operation, recording more than 15 lakh passenger journeys and over 2,500 wagons of freight delivered to Sairang. The railway line and Sairang Railway Station were inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on September 13, 2025. The line connects Bairabi with Sairang near Aizawl through four new stations—Hortoki, Kawnpui, Mualkhang and Sairang. During the first year, passenger services on the route completed more than 1,100 trips, with occupancy exceeding 100% on every trip. Ticket sales crossed Rs 54 crore. Three long-distance services currently connect Sairang with Guwahati, Kolkata and Delhi, while the Sairang-Silchar passenger service, introduced in January 2026, provides an additional link with Assam’s Barak Valley. According to the Ministry of Railways, Sairang Railway Station handled more than 5.54 lakh passenger movements during the first year of operation, averaging around 3,300 passengers a day. (Photo Courtesy: Ministry of Railways/PIB) The tri-weekly Sairang-Kolkata service recorded average occupancy of over 140%, while the daily Sairang-Guwahati service averaged above 110%. The Sairang-Anand Vihar Rajdhani Express recorded average occupancy of more than 145%, informed a press release from the Union Ministry of Railways via PIB. Sairang Railway Station handled more than 5.54 lakh passenger movements during the year, averaging around 3,300 passengers a day, it added. Freight movement Freight operations began on September 14, 2025, with the first cargo train carrying more than 26,000 bags of cement from the STAR Cement siding at Tetelia near Guwahati. More than 2,500 wagons of freight have since been delivered at Sairang, around 70% comprising construction materials such as cement, stone and sand. Other consignments included foodgrains, fertilisers and automobiles. In December 2025, the first automobile consignment—119 Maruti cars from Changsari near Guwahati—arrived at Sairang by rail. In all, 156 wagons carrying automobiles were delivered during the year. The first parcel consignment from Sairang was booked on September 19, 2025, carrying anthurium flowers to Delhi in the parcel van of the Sairang-Anand Vihar Rajdhani Express. Tourism and connectivity The direct rail services have expanded travel options between Mizoram and major centres including Delhi, Kolkata, Guwahati and Silchar, providing connectivity for passengers travelling for education, healthcare, business and other purposes. Figures cited in the release noted that tourism in Mizoram has increased by more than 86% since the introduction of rail connectivity. The 51.38-km line comprises 153 bridges, including 55 major and 88 minor bridges and 10 road overbridges/road underbridges. Six bridges exceed 70 metres in height, with the tallest measuring 114 metres. The alignment also includes 45 tunnels stretching nearly 16 km. The line has extended the national railway network to Sairang, bringing rail connectivity closer to Aizawl...

national_raw_news.content: Ministry of Railways 50 Kilometres, Countless Beneficiaries: Mizoram’s Railway Lifeline Completes One Year of Success Within Just One Year, Bairabi-Sairang Railway Line Transforms Travel, Tourism and Logistics in Mizoram, Opening New Horizons for the Hill State Posted On: 13 SEP 2026 11:27AM by PIB Delhi On 13 th September 2025, the inauguration of the 51.38 km Bairabi-Sairang railway line and the Sairang Railway station by Hon’ble Prime Minister of India, Shri Narendra Modi, opened a new chapter of progress and development for Mizoram. Within just one year, the railway line has brought about transformative development in this remote hill state, and has transformed from just a line on the railway map into a gateway towards improved mobility, greater access to markets, enhanced tourism and new opportunities. 🛤️ Bairabi–Sairang railway line turns One, opening doors to endless opportunities https://t.co/BNXtbuzpOr — Ashwini Vaishnaw (@AshwiniVaishnaw) September 13, 2026 The Milestone: When the Rails Reached the Hills For generations, Mizoram’s difficult terrain made long-distance movement heavily dependent on roads, making travel very time consuming, uncomfortable and unrealiable. The commissioning of the Bairabi-Sairang new railway line completed changed the scenario. (The Bairabi-Sairang line carries the national railway network across Mizoram’s challenging hill terrain) The Bairabi Sairang railway line is an engineering marvel, traversing the steep hills, deep valleys and gorges of Mizoram. The project comprises 153 bridges, including 55 major bridges, 88 minor bridges and 10 Road Over Bridges/Road Under Bridges. As many as six bridges exceed 70 meters in height, with the tallest rising up to 114 meters, which is 42 metres taller than Delhi’s Qutub Minar. The alignment also passes through 45 tunnels stretching over almost 16 kilometres. The rail corridor connects the national railway network onwards from Bairabi with the four newly developed stations of Hortoki, Kawnpui, Mualkhang and finally the Sairang railway station, thereby completing rail connectivity to the very threshold of Aizawl, the capital of Mizoram. Thus, the inauguration of the Bairabi Sairang Railway Line on 13 th September 2025 fulfilled a long cherished dream of the people of Mizoram, and brought reliable railway passenger and freight services close to the State’s largest centre of population, administration, education and commerce. (Sairang station became Mizoram’s new passenger and logistics gateway to the national railway network) Passenger Mobility: The Numbers tell a story of trust Three important long distance train services now connect the capital of Mizoram with the cities of Guwahati, Kolkata and Delhi. The Sairang – Anand Vihar Rajdhani Express gave Mizoram its first direct premium railway connection with the national capital, while the Guwahati and Kolkata services created dependable links with major educational, commercial and medical centres across the eastern and northern parts of the country. Further, the Sairang – Silchar passenger train service, which was inaugurated by Hon’ble Union Minister of Railways, Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw in January 2026, provided a regular and reliable passenger train service connecting Sairang with the Barak Valley of Assam. national_raw_news.content: Rashtriya Raksha University successfully concludes BRICS AML/CFT capacity building programme Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर Rashtriya Raksha University successfully concludes BRICS AML/CFT capacity building programme ANI | Updated: Sep 13, 2026 16:58 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], September 13 (ANI): Rashtriya Raksha University (RRU), an Institution of National Importance, on Sunday hosted the valedictory ceremony marking the successful conclusion of the five-day BRICS Anti-Money Laundering (AML) and Countering the Financing of Terrorism (CFT) training programme on emerging risks, FATF methodologies, and BRICS best practices. According to the Ministry of Home Affairs press release, the international capacity-building initiative brought together delegates and experts at RRU’s Lavad campus to strengthen cross-border financial security and compliance frameworks. Bimal N. Patel, Vice-Chancellor, RRU, delivered the Welcome Address, while Suhel Ajaz Khan, Additional Secretary, Counter-Terrorism Division, Ministry of External Affairs (MEA), Government of India, and Her Excellency Lalatiana Accouche, High Commissioner of the Republic of Seychelles to India, addressed the gathering as Guest of Honour and Chief Guest, respectively. Delivering the Welcome Address, Patel highlighted the university's commitment to extending security education, research, and innovation to the Global South, the release said. Emphasising RRU’s unique integrated approach that brings defence and police forces under one academic platform, he noted that global security fundamentally relies on the collective safety of individual nation-states. Patel also extended an open invitation to participating nations to collaborate with India and RRU to establish similar security laboratories and centres of excellence in their home jurisdictions. In his Special Address, Suhel Ajaz Khan reflected on the 25th anniversary of the 9/11 attacks, underscoring that terrorism remains a grave global threat heavily reliant on illicit finance. He stressed the urgent need for international systems to adapt to digital platforms, virtual assets, and complex corporate structures. The release highlighted that Khan outlined the Financial Action Task Force’s (FATF) 11 Immediate Outcomes spanning financial intelligence, beneficial ownership, and targeted financial sanctions as foundational benchmarks for global readiness. He also highlighted India’s robust AML/CFT ecosystem, its high technical compliance recognised in the 2024 FATF Mutual Evaluation, and the critical role of multilateral cooperation within the BRICS framework. Addressing the delegates, Lalatiana Accouche commended the enduring partnership between India and Seychelles, coinciding with the 50th anniversary of their diplomatic relations. She emphasised that because modern criminal networks are sophisticated and transnational, law enforcement agencies must continuously adapt their investigative and analytical methodologies. Highlighting the shared maritime security interests in the Indian Ocean, she praised international capacity-building initiatives not merely as a transfer of knowledge but as a vital mechanism for empowering professionals, strengthening institutions, and building sustainable, cross-border networks, the release said. Speaking to the delegates in one of the sessions, Smarak Swain, Director of the FATF Cell, Ministry of Finance, stated, “The BRICS leadership had resolved in the Kazan Declaration of 2024 and in the Rio de Janeiro Declaration of 2025 to enhance dialogue on anti-money laundering and countering the financing of terrorism. national_raw_news.content: Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment Strengthening Welfare Healthcare Support And Dignified Living For Senior Citizens More Than 2.88 Lakh Senior Citizens Benefit From Essential Care And Support Services; 142 New Senior Citizen Homes Sanctioned 228 Camps Cover Over 4.91 Lakh Beneficiaries, With Around 23.93 Lakh Free Assistive Living Devices Distributed Posted On: 13 SEP 2026 12:31PM by PIB Delhi The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment is continuously taking measures to strengthen welfare, protection, healthcare support and dignified living for senior citizens. These efforts focus on expanding institutional care, providing essential services and improving access to assistive living devices for elderly persons. Giving details, Secretary, Ministry of Social Justice And Empowerment, Shri Sudhansh Pant said that more than 2.88 lakh senior citizens have benefited from the provision of shelter, nutritious food, healthcare services, physiotherapy, recreation and other essential support facilities. These services support their daily needs and promote their physical well-being and quality of life. He said that 142 new Senior Citizen Homes have been sanctioned across different parts of the country, to expand institutional care and support infrastructure adding the additional homes will strengthen access to care and essential support for elderly persons. The Secretary added that to enhance accessibility and independent living, 228 camps were organised covering more than 4.91 lakh beneficiaries whileas around 23.93 lakh free assistive living devices were distributed. These included wheelchairs, hearing aids, walking sticks and spectacles for eligible senior citizens belonging to Below Poverty Line (BPL) categories and low-income groups supporting mobility, communication and participation in everyday activities, he added. Shri Pant added that to further strengthen access to information, a Senior Citizen’s Welfare Portal was launched by the Hon’ble President of India as a one-stop solution for information dissemination that provides a common platform for accessing information related to senior citizens’ welfare. The Secretary said that these measures reinforce the Ministry’s commitment to supporting senior citizens through accessible care, improved welfare infrastructure and assistance that enables them to lead dignified and independent lives. ***** PR-113- TAR/KV/GA/RK (Release ID: 2309671) Visitor Counter : 210 Read this release in: Urdu , हिन्दी , Tamil Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment Strengthening Welfare Healthcare Support And Dignified Living For Senior Citizens More Than 2.88 Lakh Senior Citizens Benefit From Essential Care And Support Services; 142 New Senior Citizen Homes Sanctioned 228 Camps Cover Over 4.91 Lakh Beneficiaries, With Around 23.93 Lakh Free Assistive Living Devices Distributed Posted On: 13 SEP 2026 12:31PM by PIB Delhi The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment is continuously taking measures to strengthen welfare, protection, healthcare support and dignified living for senior citizens. national_raw_news.content: Significance of interdisciplinary, evidence-based research in Ayurveda highlighted at Jamnagar workshop Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर Significance of interdisciplinary, evidence-based research in Ayurveda highlighted at Jamnagar workshop ANI | Updated: Sep 13, 2026 08:34 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], September 13 (ANI): The Institute of Teaching and Research in Ayurveda (ITRA), Jamnagar, an Institution of National Importance under the Ministry of Ayush, organised a three-day intensive workshop which highlighted the importance of interdisciplinary and evidence-based research for generating scientifically validated knowledge and strengthening the scientific foundation of Ayurveda . The workshop, ‘Understanding Health and Wellness through Microbiome Research ’ held from September 9 to 11, aimed to familiarise participants with emerging developments in microbiome research and explore its potential relevance to health, wellness and preventive healthcare from an Ayurvedic perspective, according to the release. Prof. Sharmila Mande, Ayush Distinguished Scientist Chair, Ministry of Ayush, and Dr. Tarini Shankar Ghosh, Assistant Professor, IIIT-Delhi, delivered sessions during the workshop and shared insights into contemporary concepts, research methodologies and emerging evidence in microbiome science. The interactions provided participants with an opportunity to understand the potential implications of microbiome research for human health. The workshop brought together Ayurvedic knowledge and contemporary microbiome science, with discussions covering areas including diet, digestion, metabolism, health promotion and individualised approaches to health and wellness. The workshop concluded with a brainstorming session led by Prof. Tanuja Nesari, Director, ITRA, to identify potential areas for collaborative and multi-centric research. Discussions explored the scientific investigation of Ayurvedic concepts such as Agni (digestion and metabolism), Ahara (diet), Prakriti, healthy lifestyle practices and Ayurvedic therapies in relation to gut microbial communities. A total of 52 faculty members and research scholars participated in the three-day workshop. The programme facilitated knowledge exchange, scientific dialogue and identification of future avenues for collaborative research. The initiative is expected to contribute to strengthening interdisciplinary research at the interface of Ayurveda and modern scientific disciplines. Microbiome research offers potential avenues for studying traditional Ayurvedic concepts through contemporary scientific frameworks and developing evidence-based approaches in areas such as preventive healthcare, nutrition, digestive health, metabolic health and overall wellness. The workshop is part of ITRA’s continued efforts to promote evidence-based, interdisciplinary and public-health-oriented research in Ayurveda , with the objective of translating traditional knowledge into scientifically validated approaches for promoting health and well-being. Among the proposals outlined by Dalela was the BRICS Troika mechanism, an arrangement intended to ensure greater continuity and coordination in the bloc’s leadership transitions between the outgoing, current and incoming chairs of the grouping. Modi also proposed a roadmap for reforming global governance structures, a theme that has featured prominently in India’s engagement with multilateral institutions in recent years as emerging economies push for a greater voice in bodies that were largely shaped in the aftermath of the Second World War. The Prime Minister’s proposals additionally included assistance measures for seafarers stranded in crisis situations, an issue that has drawn increasing international attention amid conflicts and geopolitical disruptions affecting global shipping routes, along with measures aimed at enhancing the negotiating capacity of the Global South, a grouping of developing nations that BRICS has increasingly positioned itself as a voice for on the world stage. Dalela’s briefing offered one of the clearest official summaries yet of the substantive agenda India has pushed during its chairship of the bloc this year, with the initiatives spanning institutional reform, economic cooperation and humanitarian concerns. national_raw_news.content: BRICS Summit Spotlights Dravidian Architecture - https://onlykashmir.in/ Facebook Instagram Pinterest X Website Youtube State National World Watch Feature Columns Corner Urdu Behind The News Satire Entertainment Sports Videos About Us Search Only Kashmir Behind The News Facebook Instagram X Only Kashmir Behind The News State National World Watch Feature Columns Corner Urdu Behind The News Satire Entertainment Sports Videos About Us Search Home National National Spotlight BRICS Summit Spotlights Dravidian Architecture By Online Editor September 12, 2026 Advertisement Mirwaiz Umar Farooq meets Iranian President and Foreign Minister in New Delhi September 13, 2026 J&K Filmmakers Win Big at IFFJK 2026 September 12, 2026 PIB Srinagar Takes Journalists on Chennai Tour September 12, 2026 J&K Approves ₹49.34 Cr Jammu Parking Projects September 12, 2026 PM Modi Pitches Key BRICS Initiatives September 12, 2026 Advertisement - Advertisement - Onlykashmir.in News Desk The 18th BRICS Summit offered visiting world leaders a striking glimpse of South India’s architectural heritage, with Prime Minister Narendra Modi welcoming delegations at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi against the backdrop of a grand corridor replicating the Rameswaram temple, built in the distinctive Dravidian architectural style. Tamil Nadu’s celebrated Ramanathaswamy Temple, on which the showcased corridor draws its design inspiration, is one of the four sites that make up the Char Dham pilgrimage circuit and is dedicated to Devadidev Mahadev, making its presence at a gathering of major world leaders a deliberate nod to one of South India’s most revered religious and architectural landmarks. The choice echoes a pattern Modi has followed at previous major international gatherings hosted by India. During the G20 Summit held in New Delhi in 2023, the Prime Minister had similarly used the venue’s design to introduce visiting leaders to the architectural artistry of the Konark Temple in Odisha, using India’s presidency of major multilateral forums as an occasion to showcase the country’s diverse regional heritage to a global audience. The Rameswaram corridor at this year’s BRICS Summit continues that pattern, offering the visiting leaders from all eleven BRICS member nations a visual introduction to South India’s temple architecture even as substantive discussions on economic and strategic cooperation unfolded around them. national_raw_news.content: J&K Approves ₹49.34 Cr Jammu Parking Projects - https://onlykashmir.in/ Facebook Instagram Pinterest X Website Youtube State National World Watch Feature Columns Corner Urdu Behind The News Satire Entertainment Sports Videos About Us Search Only Kashmir Behind The News Facebook Instagram X Only Kashmir Behind The News State National World Watch Feature Columns Corner Urdu Behind The News Satire Entertainment Sports Videos About Us Search Home Spotlight Spotlight State J&K Approves ₹49.34 Cr Jammu Parking Projects By Online Editor September 12, 2026 Advertisement Mirwaiz Umar Farooq meets Iranian President and Foreign Minister in New Delhi September 13, 2026 J&K Filmmakers Win Big at IFFJK 2026 September 12, 2026 PIB Srinagar Takes Journalists on Chennai Tour September 12, 2026 J&K Approves ₹49.34 Cr Jammu Parking Projects September 12, 2026 PM Modi Pitches Key BRICS Initiatives September 12, 2026 Advertisement - Advertisement - Onlykashmir.in News Desk The Jammu and Kashmir Government, led by Chief Minister Omar Abdullah, has accorded administrative approval for two major parking infrastructure projects in Jammu city at a combined estimated cost of ₹49.34 crore, a move aimed at easing the persistent traffic congestion that has become a familiar challenge in the winter capital’s busier commercial areas. The approved projects include a Parking-cum-Commercial Complex at Parade and a Multilevel Car Parking facility at SMGS Hospital, two locations that have long struggled with inadequate parking capacity relative to the volume of vehicular traffic and footfall they see on a daily basis. Officials said the projects are intended to provide modern, organised parking facilities at these key locations, easing congestion and improving overall traffic management in the city. The new facilities are also expected to promote better utilisation of available urban space and support planned, sustainable urban development, an approach the government has increasingly emphasised as Jammu continues to grow and its existing infrastructure comes under greater strain. Officials added that the parking infrastructure will offer greater convenience to commuters, visitors and residents alike, particularly in areas that routinely witness heavy vehicular movement and acute parking pressure during peak hours.
